14.0 JOURNALS, RUN HISTORY, NOTES AND LEARN

14.1 The journal file

One journal per item, beside documents and never inside them (D-10). One JSON object per line (JSON Lines), added and never rewritten, readable in VS Code.

journal/scripts/curve-stitch/manyRowsColumns.jsonl
{"time":"2026-11-02T14:03:11Z","kind":"run","run":"r00041","source":"runs/r00041.js","picture":"runs/r00041.png","changed":"+3 -1 lines"}
{"time":"2026-11-02T14:05:40Z","kind":"note","text":"Offset 3 makes the middle rows twist. Keep.","about":"r00041"}
{"time":"2026-11-02T14:06:02Z","kind":"mark","run":"r00041"}
{"time":"2026-11-02T15:20:00Z","kind":"study","study":"s0007","file":"studies/s0007.json"}
{"time":"2026-11-02T15:31:12Z","kind":"explanation","about":["r00041","r00042"],"text":"...","approved":true}
{"time":"2026-11-03T09:00:00Z","kind":"commit","hash":"9f6040d","runs":["r00041","r00043"]}
DR-14.1A journal's folder holds its runs (runs/rNNNNN.js and .png) and studies (studies/sNNNN.json). Run and study numbers are per item, never reused.
DR-14.2Appends go through the service (journal.append), which writes the line with a single append call, so a crash cannot damage earlier lines; a torn last line is ignored on read.
DR-14.3Journals are in git like everything else, except runs/ pictures older than the retention period, which may be thinned (DR-14.6).

14.2 Run history

on each run of a script (or generator, from Draw):
  text = the source as loaded;  h = hash(text)
  if h == the hash of this item's last run: nothing new; done
  number = next run number
  write runs/rN.js = text
  after the first frame: write runs/rN.png = a 240 px picture of the drawing
  append { kind: "run", run: rN, changed: line diff counts against the last run, error?: the run's error }
DR-14.4Capture is at run time (P-23): every run whose source changed, whether or not the owner saved in VS Code, committed, or marked anything.
DR-14.5The history panel lists runs newest first with their pictures; for any run: Run (draw that version, file untouched), Diff (with the run before), Against now, Restore (replace the file's text, itself a recorded change), Mark, Note.
DR-14.6Retention (O-15): unmarked runs older than the period (default 30 days) are thinned to the first and last of each working session (runs less than 30 minutes apart are one session). Marked runs, and runs a commit entry names, are kept for good.
DR-14.7An old run is executed against today's kernel and draw code; the panel says so, and shows the stored picture beside the new one, so a difference is visible (V1's Script history cannot show the stored picture).

14.3 Notes

One global Notes command opens the journal of whatever is open (script, generator, figure, or the active layer by lid) with a box to add a note; notes show in the item's history and in the Notes popup beside the header comment.

14.4 Learn

Learn request (only when the owner presses for it):
  what:  { kind: "runs", a: rN, b: rM }         the code diff and both pictures
       | { kind: "regression", item, change }    the approved and new pictures and geometry summary, and the diff of the code since approval
       | { kind: "ideabook", image }             the image, and the routines catalogue: "draft a hint"
  shown first: exactly what will be sent, and to which service (O-13); the owner presses Send or Cancel
  reply: a draft explanation or draft script, shown in an editor; the owner edits, then Approve or Discard
  Approve: appends { kind: "explanation", approved: true } (or saves the draft script as a new item, never over an existing one)
DR-14.8Nothing leaves the machine without the owner's press, every time; there is no automatic or background Learn (D-13).
DR-14.9Nothing Learn returns is written to a journal or the library until approved. Discarded drafts are not kept.
DR-14.10A Learn draft script is a hint (section 16.4) or a new playpen script; it never replaces a file the owner wrote.

14.5 Acceptance tests

AT-14.1Run a script, change one line in VS Code, save, run: the history has two runs, the second's Diff shows the one line, both pictures shown.
AT-14.2Kill the service mid-append: the journal reads back with every complete line.
AT-14.3Learn with no network: the request is refused with a clear message; nothing is written.

15.0 SWEEP

FS 6.15. A parameter study in two forms, both acting on the open object (Draw) or the active layer (Figures).

values(setting, from, to, count):
  base = setting.min if defined else 0;  step = setting.step (int: 1)
  for i in 0..count-1: raw = from + (to - from) * i / (count - 1)
    v = base + round((raw - base) / step) * step;  clamp to [min, max];  drop repeats
grid (form 1):     one setting: up to 16 values, 4 across; two settings: values1 across, values2 down, at most 16 cells
slideshow (form 2): frames = one-setting run, or the two-setting grid in an order (O-12):
                     "rows" (setting 1 changes fastest) or "snake" (alternate rows reversed, so neighbours differ by one step)
state machine:     Playing --Pause--> Paused --Play--> Playing;  Paused --Back--> previous frame (stays Paused)
                   Playing --(frame time 5..10 s)--> next frame;  any --Stop--> Stopped (applies the frame shown)
                   clicking a grid cell applies that cell
DR-15.1Pictures are made off screen by the renderer (FR-6.11.8), from private evaluations; the open document is not changed until a choice is applied.
DR-15.2Applying is one command ("Sweep: steps 24, offset 3"), undoable.
DR-15.3The seed is held fixed across a sweep of a random generator (FR-6.15.4).
DR-15.4Frame time is a setting, 5 to 10 s, default 7 s; Back during Playing pauses and goes back one frame.
DR-15.5Save as study (FR-6.16.7): the study file holds target, starting settings (a copy), the swept settings and their values, form, order, frame time, seed and the chosen cell; replay offers "as it was" and "as it would look now".

15.1 Acceptance tests

AT-15.1Sweep Cycloid's factor 2 to 5 in 4 pictures and nodes 60 to 120 in 4: a 4 × 4 grid labelled with both values; click a cell: the object takes both values; Undo restores them.
AT-15.2Slideshow at 5 s: Pause holds; Back shows the previous frame; Stop applies the frame shown.
AT-15.3A saved study replayed "as it was" after the figure has changed shows the original pictures.

16.0 REGRESSION, CHECKS, ROBUSTNESS AND IDEABOOK HINTS

16.1 The regression harness

V1 has one (npm run test:regression, 199 items); V2 is built with it from the first checkpoint (D-9).

for each item (generator at defaults, saved figure, legacy script, Ideabook hint):
  evaluate (or run in the host) twice
  geometry = every stitch's two ends, rounded to 0.01 document units, per layer, in order
  fingerprint = sha1(geometry text);  picture = 240 px PNG
  stable = both runs give the same fingerprint (and, with no geometry, the same picture)
compare with tests/regression/approved.json + approved/<item>.png:
  no approved copy: listed as "not yet approved", does not fail
  unstable: listed, not compared
  geometry present: changed if the stitch count or fingerprint differs
  geometry absent (a painting script): changed if more than 0.1 % of pixels differ by more than 8 levels
  error status changed: changed
report: tests/regression/report.html, approved and new pictures side by side, changes only
accept [name]: replace the approved copy of matching items (all if no name); commit tests/regression/
DR-16.1The harness is one command and runs before every review and at every checkpoint; nothing merges with an unexplained change (FR-6.17.2).
DR-16.2For the V1-to-V2 comparison (FR-6.17.4), geometry is compared within a tolerance of 0.5 px per point after aligning bounds, since exact reproduction is not required (D-4); the report lists items outside it for the owner's eye.
DR-16.3Approved copies made on one platform may differ in pictures on another (anti-aliasing, fonts); geometry is the deciding comparison; pictures only for items with no geometry, and a platform's pictures can be re-accepted wholesale.

CheckWhat it doesWhen

16.3 Robustness

DR-16.4Budget (FR-6.18.2): an evaluation may produce at most 500,000 stitches and take at most 2 s of compute per layer (settings); past either it stops, the layer shows "stopped: 1,240,000 stitches asked for; the setting nodes (2,000) is the likely cause", and the rest of the figure draws.
DR-16.5Evaluation of a layer may run in a Web Worker when it is expected to exceed 50 ms (by its last time), so the page stays responsive; results are the same either way.
DR-16.6Kept versions (FR-6.18.4): on each save the previous file is kept as <name>.v1.json ... .v5.json, the oldest dropped.
DR-16.7Integrity check with repair (FR-6.18.5): listed problems each offer a repair (drop the dangling reference, re-attach to the nearest feature, renumber), applied as one undoable command.

16.4 Ideabook hints

DR-16.8A hint is a document (FR-6.22.2) stored as library/ideabook/<category>/hints/<image name>.json, with a header note: what the image seems to be, what it is built from, what was guessed, and, for a numbered Figure, the StringThing function that drew it.
DR-16.9The link is by name; characters the server will not serve in a file name (& , # ? % + ;) are written as _ (V1's rule).
DR-16.10The Ideabook view shows the image and the hint side by side when the window is wide enough, toggled otherwise; Open as figure copies the hint into a new figure.
DR-16.11V1's 282 hint scripts are converted by the importer (FS 6.10) as its first large test; each converts or is listed with why not.
